record.paper_title: On Some Open Problems in Monotonic and Conservative Learning
record.context_brief: bounded mind changes versus conservative text learning
record.original_question: Does there exist an indexed family of languages over the natural numbers with the following property for learning from texts? A text for a language contains all and only the elements of the language, presented one at a time in arbitrary order with repetitions allowed. A learner succeeds when its sequence of language-index hypotheses stabilizes to a correct index. A conservative learner changes its conjecture only when the data seen so far contradict the current hypothesis. Is there an indexed family that can be learned from texts with only a bounded number of mind changes, in fact with at most two mind changes, but cannot be learned conservatively from texts?

evidence.quote: Lange and Zeugmann [LZ93] asked whether there exists an indexed family which can be learned from texts using only a bounded number of mind changes, but cannot be conservatively learned from texts.

In this paper we answer this question positively by showing that there exists an indexed family which can be learned from texts using at most two mind changes, but which cannot be conservatively learned.

artifact.category_tag: inductive inference / language learning in the limit
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L} = (L_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ be an indexed family of recursive languages, where each $L_i \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is uniformly decidable in $i$. A text for a language $L$ is an infinite sequence $t = t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ such that $\{t_n : n \in \mathbb{N}\} = L$ (repetitions allowed, in arbitrary order); write $t[n] = (t_0, \dots, t_{n-1})$ and $\mathrm{content}(t[n]) = \{t_0, \dots, t_{n-1}\}$. A learner is a computable function $M$ mapping finite initial segments of texts to indices in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{?\}$. The learner $M$ converges on text $t$ to index $e$ if $M(t[n]) = e$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The family $\mathcal{L}$ is learnable from text by $M$ if, for every $i$ and every text $t$ for $L_i$, $M$ converges on $t$ to some index $e$ with $L_e = L_i$.

Define:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $M$ learns $\mathcal{L}$ with at most $k$ mind changes if, additionally, for every text $t$ for some $L_i$, the number of indices $n$ with $M(t[n]), M(t[n+1]) \in \mathbb{N}$ and $M(t[n]) \neq M(t[n+1])$ is at most $k$.
  \item $M$ learns $\mathcal{L}$ conservatively if, additionally, for every text $t$ for some $L_i$ and every $n$, whenever $M(t[n]) = e \in \mathbb{N}$ and $\mathrm{content}(t[n+1]) \subseteq L_e$, then $M(t[n+1]) = e$.
\end{itemize}

Question: Does there exist an indexed family $\mathcal{L}$ of recursive languages over $\mathbb{N}$ that is learnable from text with at most two mind changes but is not conservatively learnable from text?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originally posed by Lange and Zeugmann (1993), was answered affirmatively: there exists an indexed family learnable from text with at most two mind changes that cannot be learned conservatively from text. This resolution is reported in the work containing the problem statement and is consistent with the standard learning-theoretic literature on conservative versus bounded-mind-change learning.
